evidence_against.relevance: Alex regularly checks on several group members, gives others treats, and has made one-on-one plans with another friend, so some behavior fits general friendliness.
There has been no explicit romantic labeling, direct statement of interest, or explicitly romantic physical contact.
Postponing two dinners without offering a concrete replacement date the following week weakens the inference of strong or active special interest.

evidence_supporting.relevance: Three initiated one-on-one plans, including an evening dinner, suggest focused interest in spending time with Jordan.
Remembering the presentation, sending encouragement, and bringing Jordan's preferred tea show personalized attention.
Repeated extended texting after group events about personal updates and possible shared activities indicates sustained individual engagement.
Alex's one-on-one planning appears relatively selective, although it is not unique to Jordan.

recommended_action.explanation: The pattern leans toward special or potentially romantic interest, but the absence of explicit signals and the postponed dinners make a low-pressure direct clarification more reliable than further inference.

uncertainty_explanation: Alex's selective one-on-one invitations, personalized attention, and sustained private conversations support A, while Alex's broader friendliness, lack of explicit romantic behavior, and failure to promptly reschedule dinners leave substantial room for B.
